column1: # THE ROSARIO DEATH REGISTERS, READ ACT BY ACT - BEGUN 13 September 2026.
# "Defunciones 1841-1860", film 1091422, DGS 4531021. 658 images, unrestricted.
# WHY THIS EXISTS: the "Indice de defunciones 1800-1888" was opened on 13 September and its third
# sequence - the one covering roughly 1840 to 1881 - runs A, B, C, D, E, F and STOPS mid-alphabet.
# There is no L section for those years anywhere. *** So the registers themselves are the only way
# in, and this is the first of the three films that cover the gap. ***
# METHOD, same as the 1882 baptisms: navigate /search/film/004531021?i=<N>, read the ark from the
# page title, assemble the DeepZoom tiles, read the MARGIN NAMES. Level 12 is the maximum here and
# a whole opening fits one screen with every margin legible.
# STRUCTURE, established on the first opening read: the acts run chronologically with the deceased's
# name in the margin; about five or six to a page. At that rate 658 images is on the order of six
# thousand acts for 1841-1860 alone. *** This is the largest single job in the archive and it is
# started, not finished. ***

column1: # RESUME AT: film 004531021, ?i=9.
# *** TWO THINGS LEARNED ON 14 SEPTEMBER THAT CHANGE THE ESTIMATE. ***
# 1. THE FILM CARRIES A "POOR COPY - WHOLE VOLUME" TARGET CARD. That is FamilySearch's own warning
#    on the filming of the entire volume, and it is the single most important fact for anyone
#    deciding whether to attempt this. The pages read so far ARE legible at level 12, but the
#    warning is there and it is theirs, not a guess.
# 2. THE FILM CONTAINS RE-SHOTS. Image i=6 is the same opening as i=5, re-photographed behind the
#    target card. So 658 images is NOT 658 openings, and the ?i= sequence cannot be assumed to
#    advance one opening at a time.
# A full opening carries about ELEVEN acts. On that rate 1841-1860 is on the order of six thousand.
# A NOTE ON WHAT A NULL HERE WOULD BE WORTH. The question this film can answer is not "where is
# Pablo Armando" - he was born in 1882, four decades later. It is whether any LERENA died at Rosario
# between 1841 and 1860, which would mean a Lerena was LIVING there long before 1882. The whole
# argument of this archive is that they were not a Rosario family; a Lerena death in the 1840s would
# be the strongest single blow against it. So the value of this read is that it can prove the
# archive wrong, and that is the reason to do it.
